label: Anne Shirley
value: Mrs. Allan is the minister's wife
unit: Mrs. Allan is the minister's wife and a trusted confidante to Anne Shirley. Their bond began on a mortifying note when Anne accidentally served Mrs. Allan a cake flavored with liniment, but Mrs. Allan offered gentle comfort and assured her it was an honest mistake. Over time, Anne frequently visits Mrs. Allan to share her joys and turn to her for guidance during times of deep grief, such as after Matthew's death. They also enjoy walking home together to discuss their shared ideals, teaching mistakes, and the true nature of friendship.

label: Appearance
value: Anne possesses a thin figure.
unit: Anne possesses a thin figure and a delicate, bright face characterized by a nice nose and solemn, limpid, luminous gray eyes that dilate when she is emotional. Her face is pale and freckled, notably featuring seven small freckles across her nose, though her cheeks are sometimes flushed with pink above a slim, milk-white throat. Her distinctive hair is famously red, sometimes styled in long braids or worn in short, silky curls. Friends occasionally describe her hair as auburn or ruddy, though at one point it turned a dull, bronzy green with red streaks.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley is an orphan
unit: An orphan from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early childhood living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and in an asylum at Hopeton before being brought to Green Gables in Avonlea. Though initially shocked to receive a girl instead of a boy, Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla agreed to adopt her, giving Anne a permanent home where she formed an instant, lifelong friendship with Diana Barry. Anne gradually won over the community despite early mishaps, including a fierce public outburst against Mrs. Rachel Lynde and an incident where she smashed a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he insulted her hair. Over the following years, Anne excelled academically under her teacher Miss Stacy, entering a bitter scholastic rivalry with Gilbert that culminated in them tying for first place on the Island's entrance exams. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she won the prestigious Avery scholarship; however, following Matthew's sudden death and Marilla's failing health, Anne chose to forego college to stay at Green Gables and care for Marilla. She took a position as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, where she founded the Village Improvement Society and formed a close bond with her student, Paul Irving. During her tenure, she accidentally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, but her quick apology helped spark a close friendship with him. Anne also played a key role in reuniting long-lost lovers Stephen Irving and Miss Lavendar Lewis, ultimately serving as an attendant at their wedding.

unit: An orphan from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early childhood living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and in an asylum at Hopeton before being brought to Green Gables in Avonlea. Though initially shocked to receive a girl instead of a boy, Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla agreed to adopt her, giving Anne a permanent home where she formed an instant, lifelong friendship with Diana Barry. Anne gradually won over the community despite early mishaps, including a fierce public outburst against Mrs. Rachel Lynde and an incident where she smashed a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he insulted her hair. Over the following years, Anne excelled academically under her teacher Miss Stacy, entering a bitter scholastic rivalry with Gilbert that culminated in them tying for first place on the Island's entrance exams. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she won the prestigious Avery scholarship; however, following Matthew's sudden death and Marilla's failing health, Anne chose to forego college to stay at Green Gables and care for Marilla. She took a position as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, where she founded the Village Improvement Society and formed a close bond with her student, Paul Irving. During her tenure, she accidentally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, but her quick apology helped spark a close friendship with him. Anne also played a key role in reuniting long-lost lovers Stephen Irving and Miss Lavendar Lewis, ultimately serving as an attendant at their wedding.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "You can punish me in any way you like, Marilla. You can shut me up in a dark, damp dungeon inhabited by snakes and toads and feed me only on bread and water and I shall not complain. But I cannot ask Mrs. Lynde to forgive me."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."

label: History
value: Charlotta served as the young maid and assistant to Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Charlotta served as the young maid and assistant to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, where she helped host tea parties for Anne Shirley and her friends. During a berry-picking trip, she confided her worries to Anne about Miss Lavendar's sudden melancholy and changed behavior. Later, after Anne helped facilitate a reunion between Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving, Charlotta watched from a window alongside Anne and celebrated as the couple walked affectionately in the garden. She then joined in the discussions and preparations for Miss Lavendar's eventual wedding at Echo Lodge.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "and they’re married safe and sound, no matter what happens now. The bags of rice are in the pantry, ma’am, and the old shoes are behind the door, and the cream for whipping is on the sullar steps."

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father when he was a baby. After coming to live at Green Gables, he frequently engaged in misbehavior, such as snatching his sister Dora's cake, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and locking Dora in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse before lying about it. After Anne disciplined him for eating forbidden jam, Davy and Dora were allowed to remain at Green Gables through the fall. Davy continued to display mischievous habits, such as ruining Anne's lemon pies prepared for a visiting author and struggling with poor table manners. However, he also bonded with Anne, seeking her guidance with his bedtime prayers, overcoming jealous feelings, and sharing stories of his good deeds with her. Following the death of Richard Keith, a trust fund was left for Davy and Dora, allowing them to stay permanently at Green Gables.

After Anne disciplined him for eating forbidden jam, Davy and Dora were allowed to remain at Green Gables through the fall. Davy continued to display mischievous habits, such as ruining Anne's lemon pies prepared for a visiting author and struggling with poor table manners. However, he also bonded with Anne, seeking her guidance with his bedtime prayers, overcoming jealous feelings, and sharing stories of his good deeds with her. Following the death of Richard Keith, a trust fund was left for Davy and Dora, allowing them to stay permanently at Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I . . . did something else today,” went on Davy in a muffled voice. “I’m sorry now but I’m awful scared to tell you. You won’t be very cross, will you? And you won’t tell Marilla, will you?”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Anne Shirley
value: Davy looks up to Anne.
unit: Davy looks up to Anne, taking her advice and even defending her picture from being drawn ugly. Though his mischievous nature leads to troublesome behavior, such as stealing food and lying to cover up locking his sister away, he confides in Anne when he misbehaves. Anne patiently corrects his moral lapses, such as explaining the wrongness of lying and lecturing him on prayers, retaining a strong affection for him despite his antics.

Diana met Anne in her garden at Orchard Slope, where the two girls swore a solemn oath of eternal friendship. Their bond was briefly interrupted when Diana's mother forbade them from playing together, but Diana secretly sent Anne a note at school. After Diana's sister Minnie May contracted severe croup while their parents were away, Anne saved the child's life, prompting Mrs. Barry to forgive Anne and allow the girls to be best friends again. Later, Diana helped Anne recover after a fall at a party and eventually brought her the news that Anne had tied for first place on the Island on the Queen's entrance examinations. As young adults, Diana and Anne active joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, where they canvassed their assigned roads and confronted local residents over civic matters. On one outing to search for a replacement platter, Diana stood by Anne through a rainstorm after Anne crashed through a duckhouse roof, remaining with her until they were freed and invited to tea. Diana later introduced Anne to Hester Gray's forgotten garden, brought chicken to help Anne save a dinner party for guest visitors, and got lost with Anne on a trip that led them to meet Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. Upon learning that Anne would leave Avonlea to attend Redmond College, Diana grieved losing her friend's constant presence, though the two reaffirmed their deep bond. Shortly before helping prepare Miss Lavendar's wedding, Diana fell in love with Fred Wright and visited Green Gables to confide her engagement to Anne.

value: Diana Barry said: “Why, I guess so,” she said frankly. “I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Yes,” said Diana, tossing her head, “but I’m sure he doesn’t like Julia Bell so very much. I’ve heard him say he studied the multiplication table by her freckles.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

value: Dora is a gentle child.
unit: Dora is a gentle, mild, and lovely child who is widely considered well-behaved, quiet, and a model of good behavior. Characterized as prim, proper, and demure, she generally speaks only when spoken to and keeps silent otherwise. She is industrious, neat, faithful, and observant, never needing to be told how to do a task twice and never forgetting her duties. In her work, such as planting and weeding, she acts carefully, systematically, and dispassionately. She approaches her studies meekly, reciting like a little machine, and remains composed even when pale.

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."

value: Gilbert Blythe said: “Not she,” said Gilbert emphatically. “I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.”

At the request of his dying sister, he married Emily Scott and took a two-week wedding trip to St. John, though he later separated from her over domestic habits and his parrot Ginger, which he had received from his dying brother. After settling in Avonlea, he angrily confronted his neighbor Anne Shirley when her cow strayed into his field, but the pair soon became friends after Anne accidentally sold his cow, confessed, and traded her own cow to make amends. Harrison later refused to donate to the Village Improvement Society and scoffed at Anne's ideals regarding school discipline. After a severe hailstorm hit Avonlea and killed Ginger, Harrison's wife Emily unexpectedly arrived in Avonlea, leading to a reconciliation between the couple.

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Sorry, miss! Sorry isn’t going to help matters any. You’d better go and look at the havoc that animal has made in my oats . . . trampled them from center to circumference, miss."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "He’s . . . he’s always talking nonsense. I got him from my brother who was a sailor. Sailors don’t always use the choicest language, and parrots are very imitative birds."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "has she gone and broken into my oats again? Well, never mind . . . never mind if she has. It’s no difference . . . none at all, I . . . I was too hasty yesterday, that’s a fact. Never mind if she has."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

value: Jane Andrews is a plain individual.

Her aims in her career are to earn her salary fairly, satisfy the trustees, and earn a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor, having once declared an intention to devote her entire life to teaching rather than marriage.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews earned a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor.
unit: Jane Andrews earned a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor and taught school in Newbridge. As a student, she accompanied Anne, Diana, and Billy to a recital at the White Sands Hotel, sharing compliments with Diana and expressing envy of the wealthy hotel guests during their ride home. After moving to town to attend Queen's Academy, Jane visited Anne at her boarding house alongside Josie and Ruby to help comfort her homesickness. Prior to starting their respective teaching positions, Jane joined Anne and Gilbert in a debate regarding whether corporal punishment is ever necessary in school. She later took part in a spring picnic walk with Anne, Diana, and Priscilla, exploring new paths and discussing Hester Gray in her forgotten garden. Active in local community efforts, Jane also accompanied Anne and Diana when they attempted to persuade Judson Parker not to allow advertisements to be painted on his fences.

unit: Jane Andrews earned a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor and taught school in Newbridge. As a student, she accompanied Anne, Diana, and Billy to a recital at the White Sands Hotel, sharing compliments with Diana and expressing envy of the wealthy hotel guests during their ride home. After moving to town to attend Queen's Academy, Jane visited Anne at her boarding house alongside Josie and Ruby to help comfort her homesickness. Prior to starting their respective teaching positions, Jane joined Anne and Gilbert in a debate regarding whether corporal punishment is ever necessary in school. She later took part in a spring picnic walk with Anne, Diana, and Priscilla, exploring new paths and discussing Hester Gray in her forgotten garden. Active in local community efforts, Jane also accompanied Anne and Diana when they attempted to persuade Judson Parker not to allow advertisements to be painted on his fences.

unit: During a visit to Orchard Slope, Josephine Barry was startled when Anne Shirley and Diana leaped onto her spare-room bed, prompting an initial furious reaction. However, after Anne visited her to apologize directly, Josephine was charmed by the girl's honesty, deciding to extend her stay and continue paying for Diana's music lessons. She later hosted Anne and Diana for a delightful week in Charlottetown during the Exhibition and continued to welcome Anne at Beechwood while Anne studied at Queen's Academy. Josephine eventually lent Anne a willowware platter that she had purchased for twenty dollars, though it was later accidentally broken during preparations for a visitor at Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "but I guess she didn’t make much of a mistake after all. If I’d a child like Anne in the house all the time I’d be a better and happier woman."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

value: Josephine Barry considers Anne to be a prime favorite.

value: During a Village Improvement Society initiative, Judson Parker planned to rent out his fence for painted advertisements.
unit: During a Village Improvement Society initiative, Judson Parker planned to rent out his fence for painted advertisements, prompting Anne, Jane, and Diana to try to talk him out of it. Though he initially refused their requests, Anne later accidentally overheard him accepting a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran near the Lake of Shining Waters. Fearing that Anne would expose his corruption, Judson agreed to abandon his advertisement plan in exchange for her silence.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis was named by her father.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis, named by her father after lavender, resided at Echo Lodge with her young assistant, Charlotta the Fourth. During a tea visit with Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, she became quiet and worn upon hearing the name of Paul Irving, the son of her former fiancé, Stephen Irving, with whom she had broken an engagement twenty-five years earlier over a silly quarrel. After Anne later visited her and discussed her past romance, Miss Lavendar agreed to meet Paul, forming a fond connection with the boy. Hearing of her lingering melancholy, Stephen Irving had Anne inquire if he might visit, and upon his arrival at Echo Lodge, he and Miss Lavendar reconciled. Following preparations at Echo Lodge, Miss Lavendar married Stephen, and the newlyweds were seen off by their guests.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "About your age I think. He ought to be older because I dreamed him long before you were born. But I’ll never let him get any older than eleven or twelve; because if I did some day he might grow up altogether and then I’d lose him."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Those curtains have not worn as well as they should, considering the price I paid. Dear me, Charlotta has forgotten to dust the stair railing again. I really must speak to her about it."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Anne Shirley
value: Miss Lavendar meets Anne
unit: Miss Lavendar meets Anne when Anne gets lost and stumbles upon Echo Lodge, where they quickly bond as intimate kindred spirits over tea, candy-making, and conversation. Anne becomes a frequent guest, bringing young Paul Irving to visit and agreeing to stay at Echo Lodge when Lavendar experiences melancholy moods. Anne also acts as a liaison between Lavendar and her past suitor, carrying messages and helping Lavendar prepare for his return.

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is a self-contained woman.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert is a self-contained, sensible woman known for her rigid conscience, strict nature, and love of neatness and order. Reserved in expressing her deep affection, she is fond of tacking morals onto her remarks to children and detests child stinginess, though she refuses on principle to criticize ministers. Although she can prove inexorable and becomes sarcastic when suffering from headaches, she has mellowed over time. She is motivated to fulfill her duty of raising and training children, striving to drill them into a tranquil uniformity of disposition while ensuring she is not eclipsed by other housekeepers. Additionally, she is skilled in domestic culinary arts, celebrated locally for her famous yellow plum preserves and three-year-old homemade currant wine.

value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for decades.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for decades without ever having brought up a child [F4, F8]. Having never forgiven her former beau, John Blythe, after a youthful quarrel, she had enjoyed a quiet life with few troubles alongside her brother Matthew [F3, F5, F6]. This simple existence changed when she agreed to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, only to be shocked when Matthew returned home with a young girl named Anne [S1, S3]. Though Marilla initially insisted the child must be sent back, she relented after learning of Anne's hard past and agreed to keep her [S3, S5, S6]. As she took on the task of raising Anne, Marilla was often tested by the girl's vivid imagination and frequent blunders, such as when Anne mistakenly confessed to losing Marilla's inherited amethyst brooch [F7, S8, S14]. Despite her strict discipline, Marilla gradually admitted to herself that she was becoming fond of Anne and came to love her deeply [S12, S28]. Her affection was solidified when Matthew suddenly passed away and Anne chose to forego her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla's failing eyesight, and manage Green Gables together [S44, S45]. Later, Marilla agreed to take in her late relative's young twins, Davy and Dora Keith, managing Davy's mischievous behavior alongside Anne [S53, S54, S58, S69]. When a neighbor's passing left Mrs. Rachel Lynde widowed, Marilla proposed that Mrs. Lynde move into Green Gables, which allowed Anne to finally pursue her college education [S73].

label: Personality
value: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet, shy, and patient man who hates being around strangers or going to places where he might have to speak. He holds a deep dread of women, with the exception of Marilla and Mrs. Rachel, and feels a mortal dread of little girls. Despite his quiet nature, he is wise, kind, and good-natured, proving to be a sympathetic listener who enjoys talkative people willing to converse without expecting him to respond. Although argument is not his strong point, he is known for clinging to his opinions with incredible silent persistency, such as when he desired to keep Anne Shirley at Green Gables. He is notably lenient and forgiving, offering love and sympathy to those around him without ever scolding.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables, having grown up when the farm's new house was built, and habitually wore a full brown beard since the age of twenty. Shy by nature, Matthew dreaded all women with the exception of his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. When he drove to Bright River to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he unexpectedly found a young girl named Anne instead. Unable to refuse her, he brought her home, and after Marilla initially insisted on returning Anne to the asylum, Matthew successfully advocated for keeping her. When Anne was later confined to her room following a conflict with Mrs. Lynde, Matthew secretly visited her to persuade her to apologize so she could rejoin the household. Over the next few years, he consistently supported Anne, giving her gifts such as a calf, chocolates, and a stylish puffed-sleeve dress he procured with Mrs. Lynde's assistance. Matthew took great pride in Anne's academic achievements, assuring her before her departure for Queen's Academy that he was prouder of her than of a dozen boys. Shortly after Anne's graduation, Matthew suffered a fatal collapse upon reading of the Abbey Bank's failure, leaving Marilla and Anne to mourn his passing.

label: History
value: Paul Irving moved from the States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea.
unit: After moving from the States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea, Paul Irving became a pupil at the Avonlea school, forming a special connection with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who considered him her favorite student. Having promised his grandmother never to associate with anyone who swore, Paul possessed a vivid imagination, creating detailed imaginary friends who lived by the shore. Over time, Paul shared discussions about grief and imagination with Anne, hosted her for tea, and was introduced by her to Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge. During a visit to Echo Lodge, Paul talked with Miss Lavendar about her imaginary dream-boy, unaware of her past romance with his father, Stephen Irving. Later, as preparations for Miss Lavendar and Stephen's wedding got underway, Paul discussed the romantic turn of events with Anne.

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: “Oh, Miss Shirley,” he cried excitedly, “you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father.”

label: History
value: Phillips served as the master of the Avonlea schoolhouse.
unit: Phillips served as the master of the Avonlea schoolhouse, where he struggled to maintain order despite resorting constantly to whipping his pupils, a position he had secured through the influence of his uncle who was a trustee. While boarding at the home of Eben Wright, he taught local children including Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe. When Anne broke a slate over Gilbert's head in response to a taunt, Phillips punished her temper by making her stand at the blackboard with a humiliating message.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a notably capable and managing woman
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a notably capable and managing woman who possesses a sharp, observant eye for everything happening beyond her own household. Characterized by a good and kindly heart, she constantly works hard, helps the poor, and never shirks her share of labor. However, she is also officious, outspoken, and critical, taking pride in speaking her mind and nagging others to ensure nobody goes wrong. Highly pious and a believer in predestination, she strictly opposes horse racing, play-acting, and higher education for women, while also holding a distinct prejudice against Americans. In addition to her pessimistic outlook and love of giving advice, she is a shrewd judge of human nature who excels at sewing and making prize-winning homemade butter and cheese.

label: History
value: When Matthew Cuthbert went to Bright River to fetch an orphan child.
unit: When Matthew Cuthbert went to Bright River to fetch an orphan child, Mrs. Rachel Lynde visited Green Gables and voiced her strong disapproval of taking in a stranger child. She later insulted Anne's appearance during a visit, which caused Anne to fly into a rage until she later delivered a dramatic apology that completely appeased Rachel. Over time, Rachel became a supportive figure, advising Marilla when Anne refused to go to school, helping Matthew acquire and sew a fashionable dress for Anne, and eventually expressing her admiration for how remarkably well Anne had matured. She frequently offered advice on local matters, though she cautioned Anne against forming a Village Improvement Society. Later, when a mix-up resulted in the local hall being painted bright blue instead of green, Rachel discovered the error. Following the unexpected arrival of Mr. Harrison's wife in Avonlea, Rachel stepped in to assist her. After the death of her own husband, Thomas, Rachel received a proposal from Marilla to move into Green Gables, an arrangement that would allow Anne to leave Avonlea and attend Redmond College.

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."

label: Personality
value: Ruby Gillis is cheerful.
unit: Ruby Gillis is a cheerful, good-tempered, and rather sentimental individual who frankly enjoys life's pleasantries, though she is also inclined to hysterics. She harbors a mortal dread of fat green caterpillars. Highly focused on romance, she thinks and talks constantly about young men, the compliments they pay her, and how crazy they are about her. Her long-held motivations include having numerous beaus and a very gay time before settling down, with plans to study to be a teacher and get married after teaching for two years.

unit: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots." Furious at the insult, Anne smashes her slate over Gilbert's head. Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand at the blackboard with a message criticizing her temper, and afterward Anne ignores Gilbert's contrite attempt to apologize.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
value: Anne and her friends re-enact Elaine.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends re-enact Elaine on a leaky flat boat, leaving Anne stranded on a bridge pile when the boat sinks. Gilbert Blythe rescues her in a dory, but Anne coldly rejects his attempt to apologize and become friends. Back home, after discussing the day's lesson on avoiding over-romanticism with Marilla, Matthew quietly encourages Anne to keep a little romance.

value: Anne suffers from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a toothache and a frustrating day, Anne mistakenly orders a pupil to throw a package into the school stove, causing an explosion of firecrackers. Later, when Anthony Pye plays a prank on her with a mouse, Anne loses her temper and whips him. Though distraught over her loss of self-control, she discovers the next morning that the punishment earned Anthony's respect.

She shares various amusing classroom incidents and transcripts of letters written by her students, concluding with a imaginative composition by her favorite pupil, Paul Irving.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne suffers from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a toothache and a frustrating day, Anne mistakenly orders a pupil to throw a package into the school stove, causing an explosion of firecrackers. Later, when Anthony Pye plays a prank on her with a mouse, Anne loses her temper and whips him. Though distraught over her loss of self-control, she discovers the next morning that the punishment earned Anthony's respect.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots." Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand at the blackboard with a message criticizing her temper, and afterward Anne ignores Gilbert's contrite attempt to apologize.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Rachel attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew stay at Green Gables. Diana rushes in seeking help for Minnie May, who has severe croup while her parents are away. Anne uses her past experience with children to treat Minnie May, saving her life, which leads Mrs. Barry to forgive Anne and allow her and Diana to be best friends once again.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a game of dares at Diana's party, Anne attempts to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof and falls, breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries her home to Green Gables, making Marilla realize how deeply she loves the girl. During her seven weeks of recovery, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school under her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
value: Matthew notices Anne's clothes are plain compared to other girls'
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
unit: Noticing how plain Anne's clothes are compared to other girls', Matthew tries to buy her a trendy puffed-sleeve dress at a Carmody shop, but gets so intimidated by the clerk that he ends up buying rakes, seed, and sugar instead. He enlists Mrs. Lynde's help to buy and sew the fashionable brown dress, which he presents to Anne on a snowy Christmas morning alongside a pair of slippers from Aunt Josephine. Anne is overjoyed by the gifts and goes on to star in the successful Avonlea Christmas concert.

value: Anne and Diana are on their way back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from Carmody, Anne and Diana discover a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing it to be her own unruly cow Dolly, Anne impetuously sells the animal on the spot to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home, she discovers Dolly safe in her pen and realizes in horror that she has mistakenly sold Mr. Harrison's cow.

Believing it to be her own unruly cow Dolly, Anne impetuously sells the animal on the spot to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home, she discovers Dolly safe in her pen and realizes in horror that she has mistakenly sold Mr. Harrison's cow.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Anne converses with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne converses with Mrs. Lynde about Marilla's improving eyesight and the upcoming Aid Society bazaar, then returns home to learn that Davy and Dora will remain with them through the fall. She recalls disciplining Davy for eating forbidden jam, after which she attends an Village Improvement Society meeting where Gertie Pye alerts everyone to Judson Parker's plan to rent his fence for advertisements. Anne, Jane, and Diana attempt to talk Judson out of it, but he refuses to change his mind.

value: Anne Shirley sets off with Diana Barry
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: After a conversation with Davy Keith at Green Gables, Anne Shirley sets off with Diana Barry to search for a replacement willow-ware platter. Their search leads them to the Copp house on Tory Road, where Anne gets stuck after crashing through the roof of a duckhouse while peering through the pantry window. Diana stays with her through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns home, frees Anne with an axe, and agrees to host tea and discuss selling her platter.

Back home, after discussing the day's lesson on avoiding over-romanticism with Marilla, Matthew quietly encourages Anne to keep a little romance.

unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

unit: Anne converses with Mrs. Lynde about Marilla's improving eyesight and the upcoming Aid Society bazaar, then returns home to learn that Davy and Dora will remain with them through the fall. chapter: v2 · I An Irate Neighbor
unit: Anne's peaceful afternoon reading Virgil is interrupted by her angry neighbor, Mr. Harrison, who confronts her after her cow strays into his oats field. Later, Marilla returns home and discusses the incident and family matters with Anne, after which Mrs. Rachel Lynde arrives and shares local gossip about incoming residents.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana are on their way back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from Carmody, Anne and Diana discover a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing it to be her own unruly cow Dolly, Anne impetuously sells the animal on the spot to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home, she discovers Dolly safe in her pen and realizes in horror that she has mistakenly sold Mr. Harrison's cow.

label: v2 · III Mr. Harrison at Home

unit: Anne visits Mr. Harrison to confess that she accidentally sold his cow, offering her own cow in exchange. unit: On the eve of beginning their teaching jobs, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate whether corporal punishment is ever necessary in school. unit: Anne and Diana continue their canvassing efforts, encountering a variety of colorful neighbors across Avonlea. label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

unit: During a game of dares at Diana's party, Anne attempts to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof and falls, breaking her ankle. chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

unit: During a game of dares at Diana's party, Anne attempts to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof and falls, breaking her ankle. During her seven weeks of recovery, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school under her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
value: Matthew notices Anne's clothes are plain compared to other girls'
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
unit: Noticing how plain Anne's clothes are compared to other girls', Matthew tries to buy her a trendy puffed-sleeve dress at a Carmody shop, but gets so intimidated by the clerk that he ends up buying rakes, seed, and sugar instead. He enlists Mrs. Lynde's help to buy and sew the fashionable brown dress, which he presents to Anne on a snowy Christmas morning alongside a pair of slippers from Aunt Josephine. Anne is overjoyed by the gifts and goes on to star in the successful Avonlea Christmas concert.

Back home, after discussing the day's lesson on avoiding over-romanticism with Marilla, Matthew quietly encourages Anne to keep a little romance.

unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that her eyesight is failing, prompting her to consider selling Green Gables. label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne suffers from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a toothache and a frustrating day, Anne mistakenly orders a pupil to throw a package into the school stove, causing an explosion of firecrackers. Later, when Anthony Pye plays a prank on her with a mouse, Anne loses her temper and whips him. Though distraught over her loss of self-control, she discovers the next morning that the punishment earned Anthony's respect.

unit: After a conversation with Davy Keith at Green Gables, Anne Shirley sets off with Diana Barry to search for a replacement willow-ware platter. Diana stays with her through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns home, frees Anne with an axe, and agrees to host tea and discuss selling her platter.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s
unit: Anne settles into student life at Queen's Academy, forming new friendships with Stella and Priscilla while keeping up her academic rivalry with Gilbert. She spends visits with Aunt Josephine at Beechwood and keeps her exams in perspective as commencement approaches.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana drive around canvassing their assigned road to raise money for painting the hall on behalf of the newly formed Avonlea Village Improvement Society. They encounter various eccentric neighbors, including grim Miss Eliza, her optimistic sister Catherine, a stressed husband in an apron, and an overly neat Mrs. White.

chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Before Marilla leaves for town with Dora, she and Anne talk with Davy about behaving well. Left alone to do chores, Anne accidentally dyes her nose red with rug dye instead of applying freckle lotion, right as Priscilla Grant unexpectedly arrives with Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne save the day by bringing chicken for dinner, and the guests enjoy a delightful meal and a walk through the woods before departing.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school
value: Marilla shows Anne three plain new dresses.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school
unit: Marilla shows Anne three plain new dresses she has made for her, disappointing Anne who longs for fashionable puffed sleeves. The following day, Anne attends Sunday school alone in her plain clothes decorated with wild flowers and finds the experience dull, especially compared to the other girls in puffed sleeves. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne gives Marilla a candid report of the day's events and services.

value: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots." Furious at the insult, Anne smashes her slate over Gilbert's head. Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand at the blackboard with a message criticizing her temper, and afterward Anne ignores Gilbert's contrite attempt to apologize.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots." Furious at the insult, Anne smashes her slate over Gilbert's head. Mr. Phillips punishes Anne by making her stand at the blackboard with a message criticizing her temper, and afterward Anne ignores Gilbert's contrite attempt to apologize.

unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

unit: Suffering from a toothache and a frustrating day, Anne mistakenly orders a pupil to throw a package into the school stove, causing an explosion of firecrackers. Later, when Anthony Pye plays a prank on her with a mouse, Anne loses her temper and whips him. Though distraught over her loss of self-control, she discovers the next morning that the punishment earned Anthony's respect.

unit: Anne converses with Mrs. Lynde about Marilla's improving eyesight and the upcoming Aid Society bazaar, then returns home to learn that Davy and Dora will remain with them through the fall. chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: After a conversation with Davy Keith at Green Gables, Anne Shirley sets off with Diana Barry to search for a replacement willow-ware platter. Their search leads them to the Copp house on Tory Road, where Anne gets stuck after crashing through the roof of a duckhouse while peering through the pantry window. Diana stays with her through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns home, frees Anne with an axe, and agrees to host tea and discuss selling her platter.

unit: During a game of dares at Diana's party, Anne attempts to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof and falls, breaking her ankle. unit: During class at the Avonlea schoolhouse, Gilbert Blythe tries to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots." chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
unit: Noticing how plain Anne's clothes are compared to other girls', Matthew tries to buy her a trendy puffed-sleeve dress at a Carmody shop, but gets so intimidated by the clerk that he ends up buying rakes, seed, and sugar instead. Anne refuses to let the home be sold, revealing her decision to forgo her college scholarship and remain in Avonlea to teach and care for Marilla. Mrs. Lynde later informs Anne that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school position for her, leading Anne to reconcile with Gilbert and become close friends with him.

unit: Anne's peaceful afternoon reading Virgil is interrupted by her angry neighbor, Mr. Harrison, who confronts her after her cow strays into his oats field. label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, the Village Improvement Society, and the hall painting project with Mr. Harrison before leaving for home. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it has been painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. The Improvers are initially devastated, but the rest of Avonlea rallies in sympathy and support for them against the Pyes.

unit: Noticing how plain Anne's clothes are compared to other girls', Matthew tries to buy her a trendy puffed-sleeve dress at a Carmody shop, but gets so intimidated by the clerk that he ends up buying rakes, seed, and sugar instead. Anne is overjoyed by the gifts and goes on to star in the successful Avonlea Christmas concert.

label: CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
value: Anne and her friends re-enact Elaine on a leaky flat boat.
chapter: CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends re-enact Elaine on a leaky flat boat, leaving Anne stranded on a bridge pile when the boat sinks. Gilbert Blythe rescues her in a dory, but Anne coldly rejects his attempt to apologize and become friends. Back home, after discussing the day's lesson on avoiding over-romanticism with Marilla, Matthew quietly encourages Anne to keep a little romance.

chapter: XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: After a conversation with Davy Keith at Green Gables, Anne Shirley sets off with Diana Barry to search for a replacement willow-ware platter. Their search leads them to the Copp house on Tory Road, where Anne gets stuck after crashing through the roof of a duckhouse while peering through the pantry window. Diana stays with her through a rainstorm until Miss Sarah Copp returns home, frees Anne with an axe, and agrees to host tea and discuss selling her platter.

chapter: XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
unit: Anne and Diana help Miss Lavendar and Charlotta the Fourth prepare for Miss Lavendar's wedding at Echo Lodge. The ceremony goes wonderfully as the sun breaks through the clouds, and the guests see off the newlyweds. Afterwards, Anne waits with Gilbert at the quiet house, where a moment of realization sparks a shift in how she perceives Gilbert and her own maturity.
